option.counterfactual: The existence of a nonlinear normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor is sufficient to construct a sequence satisfying all the conditions defining some member of G.
option.approach: Analyze positive decompositions of the identity and ask whether nonlinearity forces arbitrarily many summands with quasitraces bounded below by one fixed constant. Then investigate whether these decompositions can be made compatible to produce a single increasing sequence.

options.counterfactual: Every normalized 2-quasitrace sends the terms of a positive series with bounded partial sums to zero, even without a linearity assumption.
options.approach: Seek a quantitative estimate bounding the number of positive summands whose quasitraces exceed a fixed threshold when their sum is at most 1. Such an estimate would immediately exclude the prescribed constant increments.

options.counterfactual: Every bounded increasing sequence in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, although its quasitrace need not be known to be linear.
options.approach: Search the available proof notes for a precise sequential order-completeness theorem and check its hypotheses against the definition in the problem. A valid theorem would make the no-least-upper-bound condition impossible independently of the increments.

options.counterfactual: Every bounded increasing sequence in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, although its quasitrace need not be known to be linear.
options.approach: Try to construct the supremum using spectral projections and finite continuous dimension, explicitly checking that the resulting element is below every self-adjoint upper bound.

options.counterfactual: Every bounded increasing sequence in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, although its quasitrace need not be known to be linear.
options.approach: Examine whether a projection dilation of the increasing sequence can be performed inside an appropriate amplification. Determine whether compression of the projection supremum produces a supremum in the original factor without assuming an unavailable continuity property.

options.counterfactual: If any positive number belongs to G, then 1/2 also belongs to G, so the only possibilities are the empty set and (0,1/2].
options.approach: Study transformations of a witnessing positive series that increase its constant quasitrace increment while preserving bounded partial sums. Combine any improvement mechanism with downward closure.

options.counterfactual: If any positive number belongs to G, then 1/2 also belongs to G, so the only possibilities are the empty set and (0,1/2].
options.approach: Investigate whether an ultraproduct attains the supremum of achievable increments and whether extremality forces that supremum to equal 1/2. Check separately that the resulting sequence still lacks a least upper bound.
